clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old Chinese woman with no significant past medical history presented with a 1-week history of gradually worsening left lower limb weakness and numbness. On admission examination, she demonstrated diffuse left lower limb weakness (MRC grade 4) affecting hip extension, adduction, knee extension, flexion, ankle plantarflexion, and dorsiflexion, with absent left ankle deep-tendon reflex and diminished proprioception and pain perception in the left lower limb distal to the mid-calf. Neurophysiologic testing at 8 days from symptom onset (EMG/NCS) suggested a plexopathy. Imaging at 8 days revealed MRI findings of bilateral cauda equina nerve root enhancement, sparing the lumbosacral plexuses. Lumbar puncture at 12 days demonstrated cytoalbuminologic dissociation (CSF protein 1.03 g/L with only 1 WBC/μL, normal opening pressure of 12 cm H2O, and negative oligoclonal bands). Comprehensive microbiological and autoimmune assays performed on blood and CSF samples were negative. CT imaging of the neck, thorax, abdomen, and pelvis showed no suspicious masses. The clinical presentation, electrophysiologic findings, imaging characteristics, and CSF profile are consistent with lumbosacral radiculopathy with cauda equina involvement, with infectious, autoimmune, and neoplastic etiologies ruled out, supporting a diagnosis of nondiabetic LRPN.

final.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old Chinese woman with no significant past medical history presented with a 1-week history of gradually worsening left lower limb weakness and numbness. On admission examination, she demonstrated diffuse left lower limb weakness (MRC grade 4) affecting hip extension, adduction, knee extension, flexion, ankle plantarflexion, and dorsiflexion, with absent left ankle deep-tendon reflex and diminished proprioception and pain perception in the left lower limb distal to the mid-calf. Neurophysiologic testing at 8 days from symptom onset (EMG/NCS) suggested a plexopathy. Imaging at 8 days revealed MRI findings of bilateral cauda equina nerve root enhancement, sparing the lumbosacral plexuses. Lumbar puncture at 12 days demonstrated cytoalbuminologic dissociation (CSF protein 1.03 g/L with only 1 WBC/μL, normal opening pressure of 12 cm H2O, and negative oligoclonal bands). Comprehensive microbiological and autoimmune assays performed on blood and CSF samples were negative. CT imaging of the neck, thorax, abdomen, and pelvis showed no suspicious masses. The clinical presentation, electrophysiologic findings, imaging characteristics, and CSF profile are consistent with lumbosacral radiculopathy with cauda equina involvement, with infectious, autoimmune, and neoplastic etiologies ruled out, supporting a diagnosis of nondiabetic LRPN.
